Virtual Therapy - Journeyman

By: Chwayitisa Futshane | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
VR is taking off in the film and gaming industries, and now the medical profession are taking interest.

Unique Selling Point:
New software is helping patients around the world to relieve mental health conditions like PTSD and Alzheimer's.
At Oxford University a new study has phobia sufferers immersed in claustrophobic or stressful situations. Professor Daniel Freedman explains, "After just 30 minutes of VR...there were large reductions in paranoia". As a sensory stimulator, carers say Alzheimer sufferers enjoy reduced agitation when using the therapy. Trialed in 50 US hospitals, it has also become a key tool in treating soldiers with PTSD.

N2K GRAPHICS 10:00:41:16 But first it’s time to find out what the world has been watching this week.
10:00:48:07 And we start with a story of pure love between two friends
10:00:55:00 English (m)
Ian: “Jock strap, legs straps.”
Matt: “Yep.” (deep breath)
Ian: “Alright – alright nice and smooth, let’s have some fun.”

10:01:19:04 When We Were Knights follows the story of base jumpers Matt Blanc and Ian Flanders.
10:01:26:02 The pair take on death defying stunts as they chase thrills around the world, capturing the memories on their GoPros
UPSOT
10:01:39:06 However the film takes a tragic turn, when Ian passes away after an accident on a routine jump
10:01:48:15 Heartbroken by the loss of his best friend, Matt decides to take Ian’s ashes on a month long road trip, in the hope of finding closure for himself and Ian’s loved ones
UPSOT
10:02:06:03 The emotional video has garnered over 800 thousand views online and has received a truly deserved Vimeo Staff Pick
UPSOT
10:02:20:12 And from inspirational friendships to inspiring people through art
UPSOT
10:02:28:15 In galleries around the world, observers are warned against handling art due to fear of damage
10:02:37:02 However after meeting a blind man at one of his exhibitions, screw painter Andrew Myers decided it was time for a change
10:02:46:09 Andrew Myers (m) English:
“Someone was walking him around and describing the art to him and I thought, well you know that’s not fair, and I didn’t tell him what it was and he walked up to it and put his hand on this piece and started feeling it and all of sudden he got this huge smile on his face. For me it was just an amazing moment, it was a blind man that could almost see for second.”
10:03:08:06 Please Touch the Art sees Andrew team up with blind artisan George Wurtzel (pron: wurt-zel) in an attempt to level the artistic playing field
10:03:17:15 By converting an old barn into a tactile art gallery, Andrew surprises George with the first piece for the gallery – a portrait… of himself
10:03:28:20 George (m) English:
“Well that obviously is a nose, I mean there’s no doubt about that –my nose is not that big, I’m sorry. I like the beard though, the beard is good, the beard is really good.”
10:03:44:16 And viewers at home clearly liked the idea as the video has racked up over 90 thousand views online
10:03:56:17 Our final video combines cooking and chemistry
10:04:00:15 Scientist Jonathan Marcus decided to try what he believes to be a world first – deep fried water
10:04:07:21 After coating the frozen ball with flour, egg and breadcrumbs, he lowers it into the deep fat fryer and the results are astonishing
UPSOT
10:04:21:15 Viewers online have flocked to video which has over 900 thousand views and counting
10:04:27:16 However this boiling hot experiment should not tried at home

NASA 10:04:44:18 In Top Search, we look back on the life of one of the greatest sportsmen the world has ever seen
10:04:51:03 Muhammad Ali (m) English:
“I would like to hear this from you and I want the world and the cameras to hear it - who's the heavyweight champion of the world?" (crowd shouting "you" and "Muhammad Ali”)
10:05:04:20 The world awoke on June 3rd to the devastating news that sporting legend and human rights activist Muhammad Ali had died
10:05:13:14 The professional boxer known as “The Greatest” passed away in Arizona after a lengthy illness
10:05:22:06 Born Cassius Clay in 1942, Ali became the first man to win 3 heavyweight boxing titles
10:05:28:24 He first hit the world stage when he won Gold at the 1960 Rome Olympics
10:05:33:20 And soared to incredible fame at the age of 22 when he defeated reigning world champion Sonny Liston
10:05:40:16 Initially known for his quick wit and good looks Ali was the ultimate showman and quickly became one of the most recognisable faces in the world
10:05:53:09 CASSIUS CLAY (m) English
"Fifteen times I've told the clown what round he's going down and this chump ain't no different. He'll fall in eight to prove that I'm great and if he keeps talking jive I'm going to cut it to five."
10:06:05:04 The world was shaken by his passing which led many to take to social media to pay their respects
10:06:12:12 The most notable of which came from his daughter Laila Ali who paid tribute on Facebook and thanked the world for their support.
10:06:21:09 And it was Ali’s fellow sports stars that were eager to pay their respects to one of the most significant sporting figures of the 20th century
10:06:30:20 World number one tennis player Serena Williams and 10 time world boxing champion Oscar De La Hoya both paid homage to the greatest.
10:06:40:09 And current and former Presidents posted on Twitter to honour the inspirational fighter
10:06:46:21 With Barack Obama praising Ali by saying he shook up the world, and the world’s better for it. Rest in peace, Champ.
10:06:55:11 But Ali was much more than a boxer…
10:06:59:01 An advocate for the rights of black Americans throughout his life, Ali believed fame and fortune were not as important as standing up for those silenced by society
10:07:09:19 He was forced to take a break from the sport in 1967 due to his refusal to fight in the Vietnam War
10:07:18:08 Muhammad Ali (m) English
“They say to me daily: "You are a prize-fighter, what's the difference?" And I like to say to those critics of the press and to the others that there's one helluva lot of difference in fighting in the ring and going to war in Vietnam.”
10:07:34:14 During this period he became a polarizing figure both in America and around the world.
10:07:42:04 While many took to the streets of his hometown of Louisville to offer their respects in person
UPSOT
10:07:47:03 It was the response online that united a world in mourning
10:07:53:13 And many online pair tribute to the champion with their artistic creations shared on Instagram
10:07:59:19 From graphic illustrations to comical sketches to intricately detailed portraits, social media united those wanting to discuss the life of a legend.



10:08:11:02 And one user event brought the legend back to life in this dramatic GIF




10:08:15:11 With tributes pouring in both online and offline, Muhammad Ali has truly cemented his place in history both in and out of the ring






UPSOT
10:08:35:08 Next, we head to space for the galaxy’s latest innovation
10:08:40:07 NASA reached a milestone recently on their mission to make living in space a lot more comfortable
10:08:47:16 Thanks to a team of experts the astronauts aboard the International Space Station have a brand new place to live – and it’s all thanks to an inflatable module
10:08:58:11 After a failed attempt at attaching the habitat in May, the team at NASA and Bigelow Aerospace wanted to try again
10:09:07:12 And this time, thankfully, the mission was a complete success
10:09:12:14 The Bigelow Expandable Activity Module or BEAM as it’s commonly known is going to stay attached to the ISS for the next two years
10:09:23:08 During that time, astronauts will gather important data about its ability to withstand radiation, space debris and extreme temperatures
10:09:33:16 If it lasts successfully for the next two years, the team hope that the technology will be applied to a much bigger plan
10:09:40:22 A plan to help humans stay in space for longer
10:0944:20 And the ISS weren’t finished there in exciting the world with their ground-breaking moves
10:09:52:04 Teaming up with Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg, the team on the ISS carried out the first live interview with the space station
UPSOT
10:10:02:01 Mark Zuckerberg English (m)
“Alright station, this is Mark Zuckerberg at Facebook. Can you hear me ok?
10:10:08:03 Astronaut Tim Kopra (m)
“Hey Mark, we read you loud and clear. It’s a pleasure to talk with you today.”
10:10:15:07 Zuckerberg invited users to send him their questions ahead of the live broadcast interview with astronauts Tim Peake, Tim Copra and Jeff Williams
10:10:26:14 The astronauts answered questions on everything from working out in order to maintain muscle mass to what kind of foods they eat
10:10:34:13 They also revealed the very special treat they had been sent by the head of SpaceX Elon Musk
UPSOT
10:10:44:01 Astronaut Tim Kopra (m)
“We know that astronaut ice cream that you buy in the gift store – that powdery stuff – yeah that’s not real but we’ve had ice cream on board when Space X came up, they delivered a bunch of ice cream in a freezer so that’s been quite the treat. I think we’re down to our last few bars, we’re trying to ration it, so that’s the real ice cream and that’s quite a treat up here.”
10:11:03:13 Zuckerberg later admitted that while Facebook’s mission is to connect the world, connecting with space was “as cool as it gets.”

N2K GRAPHICS 10:11:16:07 Still to come: we explore how virtual reality is becoming a tool for psychotherapy and the artistic weird web trend taking the internet by storm

N2K GRAPHICS 10:00:14:20 Next, how virtual reality therapy is transforming lives across the world.
10:00:21:08 Virtual reality has already revolutionised the gaming industry, allowing players to immerse themselves in incredible new worlds built with a dazzling attention to detail
10:00:32:21 But, the technology is now being adapted to become a rather unlikely tool.
10:00:37:23 Scientists across the globe have been experimenting with VR to provide therapy for some serious mental health issues.
10:00:45:22 And thanks to years of intricate research, many issues are now being addressed in ground-breaking ways
UPSOT
10:00:58:22 For example, for many people everyday situations, such as riding on an underground train, can trigger a disproportionate response
10:01:07:10 But, thanks to a team of experts at Oxford University these people may no longer have to worry
10:01:13:18 A simulated trip on the London Underground in virtual reality has been created to help sufferers
10:01:20:03 As part of the study, 30 patients took part in a half hour session to face their fears.
10:01:25:17 Seven simulated journeys were carried out in a specialised virtual reality lab
10:01:31:09 They were then tested for their responses when faced with travelling in both a train and a lift.
10:01:42:13 Professor Daniel Freeman reveals how each patient experienced more pressure throughout the treatment
10:01:48:10 But so far, Professor Freeman and his team have generated some very positive results
10:01:53:19 Daniel Freeman (m) English:
“From just 30 minutes in VR using the right techniques, there were large reductions in paranoia. Immediately afterwards, over half the patients no longer had severe paranoia. Importantly, the benefits transferred to the real world.”
10:02:09:19 And it is hoped that one day the VR treatment will be escalated into a full clinical trial
UPSOT
10:02:16:21 But travelling on a packed London train is only one of the experiences that many struggle with
10:02:23:06 Survivors of trauma suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder can have it even worse.
10:02:30:15 Whilst this may look like a scene from Call of Duty – it couldn’t be further from a game
10:02:36:13 It is in fact a simulation from the Bravemind programme developed by the Institute of Creative Technologies
10:02:45:00 The ultimate aim for the team is to recreate battlefield experiences to help U.S soldiers suffering from PTSD
10:02:53:18 Director of Medical Virtual Reality Skip Rizzo reveals how big VR’s role is in providing this much-needed therapy
10:03:02:23 Professor Skip Rizzo (m) English
“VR is an evocative technology. It can bring out emotions that sometimes can’t come out in other ways and this is where VR shines. You can put people in simulations that bring up an emotion and then teach them ways to deal with that emotion in an appropriate fashion.”
UPSOT
10:03:25:05 And thanks to the team’s hard work, the Bravemind programme has now been introduced into more than 50 hospitals across the US
10:03:33:11 VR Therapy isn’t just for extreme cases though - it can also be helpful in treating day to day phobias
10:03:40:01 This service from the Virtually Better clinic in the U.S. helps patients to overcome their fear of flying
10:03:47:04 A short journey from the airport lounge to the seat of the plane seems simple enough for most
10:03:53:05 But for those who dread flying, this experience is associated with beating hearts, sweaty palms and severe anxiety
10:04:01:19 By taking patients on simulated flights they can confront their fears with the guidance of a virtual therapist
10:04:08:19 A life-changing experience for many who are held back by this particular phobia
10:04:14:11 And it doesn’t stop there - Virtually Better also has similar programmes to help people with phobias of lifts and heights
UPSOT
10:04:30:07 But whilst VR is proving helpful in overcoming fears – it’s also helping to stimulate minds.
10:04:36:13 This Virtual Forest from Alzheimer’s Australia Vic aims to engage dementia sufferers
10:04:43:07 The therapy immerses them in a calm, peaceful world where they can hear butterflies fluttering and watch the snow fall
10:04:50:16 The sensory therapy application stimulates their senses and allows for them to interact with the virtual world for 30 minutes
10:04:58:24 For residents who are highly agitated and find it difficult to engage for even five minutes, this experience - according to consultant Juanita - can be a revelation
10:05:09:15 Juanita Bekinschtein (f) English
“The virtual world will give a person living with a cognitive disability an enormous amount of possibilities like feel good about themselves, have some control in your life, feel important, feel valued because any time we are taking their opinions they feel valued and their self esteem is going up immediately. With every role being taken from them this is giving it back and that is priceless. It is priceless.”
10:05:47:22 Using state-of-the-art gaming technology, Unreal Engine 4, the designers have been able to create a fully immersive virtual environment
10:05:58:18 One they hope will provide dementia care on multiple platforms
10:06:04:07 From helping stressed soldiers and paranoid tube travellers to stimulating the minds of the elderly, VR is completely changing psychological therapy
10:06:15:07 Innovations in the field have already helped a wide spectrum of people – and its continued development promises a renewed hope to many more.
WEIRD WEB

YouTube / Seb Lester



[credit]
Instagram / Seb Lester



[credit]
Vimeo / Seb Lester and Johann Chan


[credit]
Instagram / Crooked Calligraphy











[credit]
Gourmet Pens


N2K GRAPHICS 10:06:28:00 Next on Weird Web, we examine the classic art trend making a comeback
10:06:34:12 Many thought smart phones and computers had killed off good handwriting.
10:06:40:13 But a new generation of social media users are helping to bring back the art of lettering
10:06:47:16 Whether it’s looping forms or blocky pop-culture logos, videos of calligraphy are gaining a new popularity online
10:06:55:08 And Seb Lester is one of the many artists thriving under this new trend.
10:07:02:22 With over a million followers on Instagram, Seb is dedicated to posting short clips of his beautiful works
10:07:11:10 Some of his most popular being his replicas of big brand logos such as Ferrari and Coca Cola with the latter gaining over 7 million views on YouTube
10:07:23:03 Seb’s work is proving to be so popular that it has even crossed over into real life.
10:07:29:16 Teaming up with the Global Street Art, Seb crafted a beautiful calligraphy mural in East London.
10:07:37:08 And the results are truly magical – adding a classical touch to a contemporary street
10:07:45:12 It’s not just Seb who is enjoying fame for his calligraphy
10:07:49:18 Shinah (pron: shin-ah) Chang also posts examples of her work on her Instagram page, Crooked Calligraphy
10:07:56:19 With over 31 thousand followers, Shinah describes her passion for the trend
10:08:01:17 Shinah Chang (f) English
“There’s something about actual ink. Like dipping a nib into an actual flowing substance and trying to control that. There’s a lot of creativity to it and you can make obviously letters look beautiful but they’re still letters and you have some boundaries and you can do quote’s and names it just was something that I really fell in love with.”
10:08:24:10 And her simple lettering made with an angled oblique pen are proving to be quite a draw online.
10:08:31:16 But part of the reason for the popularity of calligraphy is down to a renewed interest in penmanship
10:08:38:18 In a 15 second Instagram video, you can see something exceptional being made right before your eyes
10:08:46:06 And it’s inspiring people to give it a go themselves - a task that’s become easier thanks to the large number of do-it-yourself videos on social media sites
10:08:57:05 All you really need is a piece of paper, a pen and your own creativity.
10:09:03:02 Though for some, the pen is no simple matter
10:09:07:12 With variations in types, nibs and inks – there are a number of blogs dedicated to the crafty little utensils
10:09:16:21 Azizah Asgarali (pron: ah-zee-zah as-gah-rah-lee) runs Gourmet Pens – a blog and Instagram page specifically dedicated to testing pens
10:09:26:09 Whether using a special Stilovite (pron: stylo-vite) Pen or just a plain old fountain pen, Azizah manages to provide an in-depth look
10:09:36:22 The Calligraphy trend isn’t just about letters though
10:09:40:09 YouTuber Connie Chen is finding fans online for her intricate drawings of animals
10:09:46:15 Using careful calligraphy, Connie is able to draw wonderfully elegant depictions of animals
10:09:53:16 And Connie says she owes her talent and inspiration to her mother
10:09:58:12 Connie Chen (f) English
“So whenever I wrote on a blank sheet of paper, if I wasn’t able to write straight, my mum would tear it down and she would ask me to restart. If any of my letters looked different than the exemplars, she would point them out to me and she’s like, ‘Connie, who do you think wrote those exemplars? It’s not a machine, it’s a person.”
10:10:20:20 At the core of Connie’s work is relaxation as many people enjoy the slow process of artistic creation
10:10:29:10 While much time is needed to produce each piece of calligraphy, the artwork is proving a soaring success for many online
10:10:38:13 And as viewers flock to watch their construction, this trend doesn’t show signs of stopping anytime soon
UPSOT
N2K GRAPHICS 10:09:28:19 That’s it for this week’s show, join us again next time on N2K, where we’ll have more stuff you need to know.
END Next time on N2K;

Rest in peace, Champ. 10:06:55:11 But Ali was much more than a boxer… 10:06:59:01 An advocate for the rights of black Americans throughout his life, Ali believed fame and fortune were not as important as standing up for those silenced by society 10:07:09:19 He was forced to take a break from the sport in 1967 due to his refusal to fight in the Vietnam War 10:07:18:08 Muhammad Ali (m) English “They say to me daily: "You are a prize-fighter, what's the difference?" And I like to say to those critics of the press and to the others that there's one helluva lot of difference in fighting in the ring and going to war in Vietnam.” 10:07:34:14 During this period he became a polarizing figure both in America and around the world. 10:07:42:04 While many took to the streets of his hometown of Louisville to offer their respects in person UPSOT 10:07:47:03 It was the response online that united a world in mourning 10:07:53:13 And many online pair tribute to the champion with their artistic creations shared on Instagram 10:07:59:19 From graphic illustrations to comical sketches to intricately detailed portraits, social media united those wanting to discuss the life of a legend. 10:08:11:02 And one user event brought the legend back to life in this dramatic GIF 10:08:15:11 With tributes pouring in both online and offline, Muhammad Ali has truly cemented his place in history both in and out of the ring UPSOT 10:08:35:08 Next, we head to space for the galaxy’s latest innovation 10:08:40:07 NASA reached a milestone recently on their mission to make living in space a lot more comfortable 10:08:47:16 Thanks to a team of experts the astronauts aboard Bigelow Aerospace wanted to try again 10:09:07:12 And this time, thankfully, the mission was a complete success 10:09:12:14 The Bigelow Expandable Activity Module or BEAM as it’s commonly known is going to stay attached to the ISS for the next two years 10:09:23:08 During that time, astronauts will gather important data about its ability to withstand radiation, space debris and extreme temperatures 10:09:33:16 If it lasts successfully for the next two years, the team hope that the technology will be applied to a much bigger plan 10:09:40:22 A plan to help humans stay in space for longer 10:0944:20 And the ISS weren’t finished there in exciting the world with their ground-breaking moves 10:09:52:04 Teaming up with Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg, the team on the ISS carried out the first live interview with the space station UPSOT 10:10:02:01 Mark Zuckerberg English (m) “Alright station, this is Mark Zuckerberg at Facebook. Can you hear me ok? 10:10:08:03 Astronaut Tim Kopra (m) “Hey Mark, we read you loud and clear. It’s a pleasure to talk with you today.” 10:10:15:07 Zuckerberg invited users to send him their questions ahead of the live broadcast interview with astronauts Tim Peake, Tim Copra and Jeff Williams 10:10:26:14 The astronauts answered questions on everything from working out in order to maintain muscle mass to what kind of foods they eat 10:10:34:13 They also revealed the very special treat they had been sent by the head of SpaceX Elon Musk UPSOT 10:10:44:01 Astronaut Tim Kopra (m) “We know that astronaut ice cream that you buy in the gift store – that powdery stuff – yeah that’s not real but we’ve had ice cream on board when Space X came up, they delivered a bunch of ice cream in a freezer so that’s been quite the treat. I think we’re down to our last few bars, we’re trying to ration it, so that’s the real ice cream and that’s quite a treat up here.” 10:11:03:13 Zuckerberg later admitted that while Facebook’s mission is to connect the world, connecting with space was “as cool as it gets.” N2K GRAPHICS 10:11:16:07 Still to come: we explore how virtual reality is becoming a tool for psychotherapy and the artistic weird web trend taking the internet by storm PART 2 N2K GRAPHICS 10:00:04:20 Coming up: the calligraphy stars of Instagram sharing their unique creativity to millions of followers FEATURE [credit] Oxford University / Daniel Freeman [credit] Skip Rizzo / Institute of Creative Technologies [credit] Virtually Better [credit] Alzheimer’s Australia Vic N2K GRAPHICS 10:00:14:20 Next, how virtual reality therapy is transforming lives across the world. 10:00:21:08 Virtual reality has already revolutionised the gaming industry, allowing players to immerse themselves in incredible new worlds built with a dazzling attention to detail 10:00:32:21 But, the technology is now being adapted to become a rather unlikely tool. 10:00:37:23 Scientists across the globe have been experimenting with VR to provide therapy for some serious mental health issues. 10:00:45:22 And thanks to years of intricate research, many issues are now being addressed in ground-breaking ways UPSOT 10:00:58:22 For example, for many people everyday situations, such as riding on an underground train, can trigger a disproportionate response 10:01:07:10 But, thanks to a team of experts at Oxford University these people may no longer have to worry 10:01:13:18 A simulated trip on the London Underground in virtual reality has been created to help sufferers 10:01:20:03 As part of the study, 30 patients took part in a half hour session to face their fears. 10:01:25:17 Seven simulated journeys were carried out in a specialised virtual reality lab 10:01:31:09 They were then tested for their responses when faced with travelling in both a train and a lift. 10:01:42:13 Professor Daniel Freeman reveals how each patient experienced more pressure throughout the treatment 10:01:48:10 But so far, Professor Freeman and his team have generated some very positive results 10:01:53:19 Daniel Freeman (m) English: “From just 30 minutes in VR using the right techniques, there were large reductions in paranoia. Immediately afterwards, over half the patients no longer had severe paranoia. Importantly, the benefits transferred to the real world.” 10:02:09:19 And it is hoped that one day the VR treatment will be escalated into a full clinical trial UPSOT 10:02:16:21 But travelling on a packed London train is only one of the experiences that many struggle with 10:02:23:06 Survivors of trauma suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder can have it even worse. 10:02:30:15 Whilst this may look like a scene from Call of Duty – it couldn’t be further from a game 10:02:36:13 It is in fact a simulation from the Bravemind programme developed by the Institute of Creative Technologies 10:02:45:00 The ultimate aim for the team is to recreate battlefield experiences to help U.S soldiers suffering from PTSD 10:02:53:18 Director of Medical Virtual Reality Skip Rizzo reveals how big VR’s role is in providing this much-needed therapy 10:03:02:23 Professor Skip Rizzo (m) English “VR is an evocative technology. It can bring out emotions that sometimes can’t come out in other ways and this is where VR shines. You can put people in simulations that bring up an emotion and then teach them ways to deal with that emotion in an appropriate fashion.” UPSOT 10:03:25:05 And thanks to the team’s hard work, the Bravemind programme has now been introduced into more than 50 hospitals across the US 10:03:33:11 VR Therapy isn’t just for extreme cases though - it can also be helpful in treating day to day phobias 10:03:40:01 This service from the Virtually Better clinic in the U.S. helps patients to overcome their fear of flying 10:03:47:04 A short journey from the airport lounge to the seat of the plane seems simple enough for most 10:03:53:05 But for those who dread flying, this experience is associated with beating hearts, sweaty palms and severe anxiety 10:04:01:19 By taking patients on simulated flights they can confront their fears with the guidance of a virtual therapist 10:04:08:19 A life-changing experience for many who are held back by this particular phobia 10:04:14:11 And it doesn’t stop there - Virtually Better also has similar programmes to help people with phobias of lifts and heights UPSOT 10:04:30:07 But whilst VR is proving helpful in overcoming fears – it’s also helping to stimulate minds. 10:04:36:13 This Virtual Forest from Alzheimer’s Australia Vic aims to engage dementia sufferers 10:04:43:07 The therapy immerses them in a calm, peaceful world where they can hear butterflies fluttering and watch the snow fall 10:04:50:16 The sensory therapy application stimulates their senses and allows for them to interact with the virtual world for 30 minutes 10:04:58:24 For residents who are highly agitated and find it difficult to engage for even five minutes, this experience - according to consultant Juanita - can be a revelation 10:05:09:15 Juanita Bekinschtein (f) English “The virtual world will give a person living with a cognitive disability an enormous amount of possibilities like feel good about themselves, have some control in your life, feel important, feel valued because any time we are taking their opinions they feel valued and their self esteem is going up immediately. With every role being taken from them this is giving it back and that is priceless. It is priceless.” 10:05:47:22 Using state-of-the-art gaming technology, Unreal Engine 4, the designers have been able to create a fully immersive virtual environment 10:05:58:18 One they hope will provide dementia care on multiple platforms 10:06:04:07 From helping stressed soldiers and paranoid tube travellers to stimulating the minds of the elderly, VR is completely changing psychological therapy 10:06:15:07 Innovations in the field have already helped a wide spectrum of people – and its continued development promises a renewed hope to many more. WEIRD WEB [credit] YouTube / Seb Lester [credit] Instagram / Seb Lester [credit] Vimeo / Seb Lester and Johann Chan [credit] Instagram / Crooked Calligraphy [credit] Gourmet Pens N2K GRAPHICS 10:06:28:00 Next on Weird Web, we examine the classic art trend making a comeback 10:06:34:12 Many thought smart phones and computers had killed off good handwriting. 10:06:40:13 But a new generation of social media users are helping to bring back the art of lettering 10:06:47:16 Whether it’s looping forms or blocky pop-culture logos, videos of calligraphy are gaining a new popularity online 10:06:55:08 And Seb Lester is one of the many artists thriving under this new trend. 10:07:02:22 With over a million followers on Instagram, Seb is dedicated to posting short clips of his beautiful works 10:07:11:10 Some of his most popular being his replicas of big brand logos such as Ferrari and Coca Cola with the latter gaining over 7 million views on YouTube 10:07:23:03 Seb’s work is proving to be so popular that it has even crossed over into real life. 10:07:29:16 Teaming up with the Global Street Art, Seb crafted a beautiful calligraphy mural in East London. 10:07:37:08 And the results are truly magical – adding a classical touch to a contemporary street 10:07:45:12 It’s not just Seb who is enjoying fame for his calligraphy 10:07:49:18 Shinah (pron: shin-ah) Chang also posts examples of her work on her Instagram page, Crooked Calligraphy 10:07:56:19 With over 31 thousand followers, Shinah describes her passion for the trend 10:08:01:17 Shinah Chang (f) English “There’s something about actual ink. Like dipping a nib into an actual flowing substance and trying to control that. There’s a lot of creativity to it and you can make obviously letters look beautiful but they’re still letters and you have some boundaries and you can do quote’s and names it just was something that I really fell in love with.” 10:08:24:10 And her simple lettering made with an angled oblique pen are proving to be quite a draw online. 10:08:31:16 But part of the reason for the popularity of calligraphy is down to a renewed interest in penmanship 10:08:38:18 In a 15 second Instagram video, you can see something exceptional being made right before your eyes 10:08:46:06 And it’s inspiring people to give it a go themselves - a task that’s become easier thanks to the large number of do-it-yourself videos on social media sites 10:08:57:05 All you really need is a piece of paper, a pen and your own creativity. 10:09:03:02 Though for some, the pen is no simple matter 10:09:07:12 With variations in types, nibs and inks – there are a number of blogs dedicated to the crafty little utensils 10:09:16:21 Azizah Asgarali (pron: ah-zee-zah as-gah-rah-lee) runs Gourmet Pens – a blog and Instagram page specifically dedicated to testing pens 10:09:26:09 Whether using a special Stilovite (pron: stylo-vite) Pen or just a plain old fountain pen, Azizah manages to provide an in-depth look 10:09:36:22 The Calligraphy trend isn’t just about letters though 10:09:40:09 YouTuber Connie Chen is finding fans online for her intricate drawings of animals 10:09:46:15 Using careful calligraphy, Connie is able to draw wonderfully elegant depictions of animals 10:09:53:16 And Connie says she owes her talent and inspiration to her mother 10:09:58:12 Connie Chen (f) English “So whenever I wrote on a blank sheet of paper, if I wasn’t able to write straight, my mum would tear it down and she would ask me to restart. If any of my letters looked different than the exemplars, she would point them out to me and she’s like, ‘Connie, who do you think wrote those exemplars? It’s not a machine, it’s a person.” 10:10:20:20 At the core of Connie’s work is relaxation as many people enjoy the slow process of artistic creation 10:10:29:10 While much time is needed to produce each piece of calligraphy, the artwork is proving a soaring success for many online 10:10:38:13 And as viewers flock to watch their construction, this trend doesn’t show signs of stopping anytime soon UPSOT N2K GRAPHICS 10:09:28:19 That’s it for this week’s show, join us again next time on N2K, where we’ll have more stuff you need to know. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): VR is taking off in the film and gaming industries, and now the medical profession are taking interest.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: New software is helping patients around the world to relieve mental health conditions like PTSD and Alzheimer's. At Oxford University a new study has phobia sufferers immersed in claustrophobic or stressful situations. Professor Daniel Freedman explains, "After just 30 minutes of VR...there were large reductions in paranoia". As a sensory stimulator, carers say Alzheimer sufferers enjoy reduced agitation when using the therapy. Trialed in 50 US hospitals, it has also become a key tool in treating soldiers with PTSD.
